Keep every row in order. Preserve all [[I]], [[B]], [[SC]] emphasis markers, [[Nnumber]] note markers and explicit source line counts. Do not return hashes; the host binds immutable hashes.", "context": {"title": "David Copperfield", "unit": 30, "heading": "CHAPTER 28. Mr. MICAWBER’S GAUNTLET", "previous_rows": [{"source_id": "en85-u030-b0091", "target": "С этими словами, отклонив наши мольбы украсить своим присутствием дальнейшее обращение пунша, миссис Микобер удалилась в мою спальню. И я, право, почувствовал, что она — благородная женщина, из тех, что могли бы стать римской матроной и совершать всевозможные героические деяния во времена общественных бедствий.", "target_id": "ru-en85-u030-b0091", "source_sha256": "882b0439786a1cac094546acd667d3947a7f2795767b2609455716a769faedbd", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "a032c8c21bb59c80045c63f1495d6102d418492204e3be745baa83f7aa0efeb4"}, {"source_id": "en85-u030-b0092", "target": "В пылу этого впечатления я поздравил мистера Микобера с сокровищем, которым он обладает. Так же поступил и Трэдлс. Мистер Микобер протянул руку каждому из нас по очереди, а затем закрыл лицо носовым платком, на котором, как мне кажется, было больше нюхательного табака, чем он подозревал. Потом он вернулся к пуншу в высочайшем состоянии восторга.", "target_id": "ru-en85-u030-b0092", "source_sha256": "1dd0f2e26675d2b42393fd27805b865707b232ba9aaf2fa57758190b10303488", "tag": "p", "target_sha256": "3eeba9f7d866c2c773d03875234ab74db5f90d0c6a620b9de4666ffcbf5dc409"}], "source_language": "English", "part": null, "book": null, "chapter": 28, "role": "chapter"}, "source_rows": [{"id": "en85-u030-b0093", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "He was full of eloquence. He gave us to understand that in our children we lived again, and that, under the pressure of pecuniary difficulties, any accession to their number was doubly welcome. He said that Mrs. Micawber had latterly had her doubts on this point, but that he had dispelled them, and reassured her. As to her family, they were totally unworthy of her, and their sentiments were utterly indifferent to him, and they might—I quote his own expression—go to the Devil.", "sha256": "a1970c0e2020f3b585810a0d3505e0d054476a7ab82ecaf9e2fcfaf5bd50e25c", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[94]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0094", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber then delivered a warm eulogy on Traddles. He said Traddles’s was a character, to the steady virtues of which he (Mr. Micawber) could lay no claim, but which, he thanked Heaven, he could admire. He feelingly alluded to the young lady, unknown, whom Traddles had honoured with his affection, and who had reciprocated that affection by honouring and blessing Traddles with her affection. Mr. Micawber pledged her. So did I. Traddles thanked us both, by saying, with a simplicity and honesty I had sense enough to be quite charmed with, ‘I am very much obliged to you indeed. And I do assure you, she’s the dearest girl!—’", "sha256": "44605127844e20d52cf30adad1a615a4a40235ab05e8101c1cd8238841bcd238", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[95]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0095", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber took an early opportunity, after that, of hinting, with the utmost delicacy and ceremony, at the state of my affections. Nothing but the serious assurance of his friend Copperfield to the contrary, he observed, could deprive him of the impression that his friend Copperfield loved and was beloved. After feeling very hot and uncomfortable for some time, and after a good deal of blushing, stammering, and denying, I said, having my glass in my hand, ‘Well! I would give them D.!’ which so excited and gratified Mr. Micawber, that he ran with a glass of punch into my bedroom, in order that Mrs. Micawber might drink D., who drank it with enthusiasm, crying from within, in a shrill voice, ‘Hear, hear! My dear Mr. Copperfield, I am delighted. Hear!’ and tapping at the wall, by way of applause.", "sha256": "e95c8f2e9449514dc80cd70e47e1251652f07af770ecffdb06aafd73338a868e", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[96]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0096", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Our conversation, afterwards, took a more worldly turn; Mr. Micawber telling us that he found Camden Town inconvenient, and that the first thing he contemplated doing, when the advertisement should have been the cause of something satisfactory turning up, was to move. He mentioned a terrace at the western end of Oxford Street, fronting Hyde Park, on which he had always had his eye, but which he did not expect to attain immediately, as it would require a large establishment. There would probably be an interval, he explained, in which he should content himself with the upper part of a house, over some respectable place of business—say in Piccadilly,—which would be a cheerful situation for Mrs. Micawber; and where, by throwing out a bow-window, or carrying up the roof another story, or making some little alteration of that sort, they might live, comfortably and reputably, for a few years. Whatever was reserved for him, he expressly said, or wherever his abode might be, we might rely on this—there would always be a room for Traddles, and a knife and fork for me. We acknowledged his kindness; and he begged us to forgive his having launched into these practical and business-like details, and to excuse it as natural in one who was making entirely new arrangements in life.", "sha256": "c3a43c74ad946b5a9d13252272ed9be77f41eaed4d29932a9cd5b42564707621", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[97]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0097", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mrs. Micawber, tapping at the wall again to know if tea were ready, broke up this particular phase of our friendly conversation. She made tea for us in a most agreeable manner; and, whenever I went near her, in handing about the tea-cups and bread-and-butter, asked me, in a whisper, whether D. was fair, or dark, or whether she was short, or tall: or something of that kind; which I think I liked. After tea, we discussed a variety of topics before the fire; and Mrs. Micawber was good enough to sing us (in a small, thin, flat voice, which I remembered to have considered, when I first knew her, the very table-beer of acoustics) the favourite ballads of ‘The Dashing White Sergeant’, and ‘Little Tafflin’. For both of these songs Mrs. Micawber had been famous when she lived at home with her papa and mama. Mr. Micawber told us, that when he heard her sing the first one, on the first occasion of his seeing her beneath the parental roof, she had attracted his attention in an extraordinary degree; but that when it came to Little Tafflin, he had resolved to win that woman or perish in the attempt.", "sha256": "6b49bd3a13249f4ec59a74df4edb9677f2b6ad0e88810ce71af20cc036383f9b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[98]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0098", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "It was between ten and eleven o’clock when Mrs. Micawber rose to replace her cap in the whitey-brown paper parcel, and to put on her bonnet. Mr. Micawber took the opportunity of Traddles putting on his great-coat, to slip a letter into my hand, with a whispered request that I would read it at my leisure. I also took the opportunity of my holding a candle over the banisters to light them down, when Mr. Micawber was going first, leading Mrs. Micawber, and Traddles was following with the cap, to detain Traddles for a moment on the top of the stairs.", "sha256": "6fe4474b9b1803743eb9fd8e2030f14bfc2dfdcd508bef1fa560960566536b05", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[99]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0099", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Traddles,’ said I, ‘Mr. Micawber don’t mean any harm, poor fellow: but, if I were you, I wouldn’t lend him anything.’", "sha256": "90acf499cf4e6b13767e3d87fccb6642e1c209320e73d86060d50f6d248f712d", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[100]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0100", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘My dear Copperfield,’ returned Traddles, smiling, ‘I haven’t got anything to lend.’", "sha256": "e57df389e56d031634898effeec2c510da79db13afddcba7d9babb2c93c803ea", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[101]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0101", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘You have got a name, you know,’ said I.", "sha256": "c5fe7ffcf3bf076edc1b6bf0a43778a513b99a93929995456d4fcfacf6d94cd5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[102]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0102", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh! You call THAT something to lend?’ returned Traddles, with a thoughtful look.", "sha256": "5c4bda7aa10f877399cd61be97eba8a8d5e138450a22a7b0e6e39f8234378f91", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[103]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0103", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Certainly.’", "sha256": "b343cfdb893b630d807f18d305ebf66771f4f6c53cd9b45f288a26d81c2974e2", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[104]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0104", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh!’ said Traddles. ‘Yes, to be sure! I am very much obliged to you, Copperfield; but—I am afraid I have lent him that already.’", "sha256": "5c736bb29a7f9aba396ee452ad4bc0ca791e3cf4ff93d1083830905bcc6cc64a", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[105]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0105", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘For the bill that is to be a certain investment?’ I inquired.", "sha256": "befeac4ae33e81101e5f3ba764acef9be2bff8e448b724f179209a6692b49255", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[106]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0106", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘No,’ said Traddles. ‘Not for that one. This is the first I have heard of that one. I have been thinking that he will most likely propose that one, on the way home. Mine’s another.’", "sha256": "3c169e5d7defc9403a65f742a3edd0950102ec759fc5bedc35c559e15b514cb9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[107]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0107", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I hope there will be nothing wrong about it,’ said I. ‘I hope not,’ said Traddles. ‘I should think not, though, because he told me, only the other day, that it was provided for. That was Mr. Micawber’s expression, “Provided for.”’", "sha256": "bc074ab246a085b3fda6eca8e6456fc2296bc267a60b33b5cb1699f2c8dc13a1", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[108]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0108", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "Mr. Micawber looking up at this juncture to where we were standing, I had only time to repeat my caution. Traddles thanked me, and descended. But I was much afraid, when I observed the good-natured manner in which he went down with the cap in his hand, and gave Mrs. Micawber his arm, that he would be carried into the Money Market neck and heels.", "sha256": "4d55527ef0263e788712f02249bb3a759f72c0d13ace198c8d2eee17ff876680", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[109]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0109", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I returned to my fireside, and was musing, half gravely and half laughing, on the character of Mr. Micawber and the old relations between us, when I heard a quick step ascending the stairs. At first, I thought it was Traddles coming back for something Mrs. Micawber had left behind; but as the step approached, I knew it, and felt my heart beat high, and the blood rush to my face, for it was Steerforth’s.", "sha256": "b8fdfb6e832b866f31d7797b372b08522a31c7df175b333ee6a28b9f7597f27b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[110]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0110", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I was never unmindful of Agnes, and she never left that sanctuary in my thoughts—if I may call it so—where I had placed her from the first. But when he entered, and stood before me with his hand out, the darkness that had fallen on him changed to light, and I felt confounded and ashamed of having doubted one I loved so heartily. I loved her none the less; I thought of her as the same benignant, gentle angel in my life; I reproached myself, not her, with having done him an injury; and I would have made him any atonement if I had known what to make, and how to make it.", "sha256": "984e9da476018e517de0cf1ecd56c581798db3d55fa99ea4b70b6d738adcd45b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[111]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0111", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Why, Daisy, old boy, dumb-foundered!’ laughed Steerforth, shaking my hand heartily, and throwing it gaily away. ‘Have I detected you in another feast, you Sybarite! These Doctors’ Commons fellows are the gayest men in town, I believe, and beat us sober Oxford people all to nothing!’ His bright glance went merrily round the room, as he took the seat on the sofa opposite to me, which Mrs. Micawber had recently vacated, and stirred the fire into a blaze.", "sha256": "b616503161d10b3c7fed10597d5cd185224a9d2743b0b1eba1f9d680bdf6d7aa", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[112]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0112", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I was so surprised at first,’ said I, giving him welcome with all the cordiality I felt, ‘that I had hardly breath to greet you with, Steerforth.’", "sha256": "2818e6145e8fe4249f98be9f17ee778fb4d93183b65cea355a38a840b74a0995", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[113]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0113", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Well, the sight of me is good for sore eyes, as the Scotch say,’ replied Steerforth, ‘and so is the sight of you, Daisy, in full bloom. How are you, my Bacchanal?’", "sha256": "fd573eb5982e61199417330cfcc5639ea90d68d031db49feb7559518fbd542a5", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[114]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0114", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘I am very well,’ said I; ‘and not at all Bacchanalian tonight, though I confess to another party of three.’", "sha256": "476e4c143ba0e1e9541aeda87220a2ee16921b6dc3934184a9e6c297daf2be8b", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[115]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0115", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘All of whom I met in the street, talking loud in your praise,’ returned Steerforth. ‘Who’s our friend in the tights?’", "sha256": "db92ef1676cf390592c11ebd632030c68d02422050cca612317d668bf0c39245", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[116]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0116", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I gave him the best idea I could, in a few words, of Mr. Micawber. He laughed heartily at my feeble portrait of that gentleman, and said he was a man to know, and he must know him. ‘But who do you suppose our other friend is?’ said I, in my turn.", "sha256": "836122588c66b6722b6da8aa1bb4943de6cd0796622976f26a9977679b2decff", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[117]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0117", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Heaven knows,’ said Steerforth. ‘Not a bore, I hope? I thought he looked a little like one.’", "sha256": "781ab8f56c7815009481bf8f3765a23e85d9aab425ae838580328dee0be3efcb", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[118]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0118", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Traddles!’ I replied, triumphantly.", "sha256": "ed58fbe6d60ac419cc364db84e56f9fd0eba6a8f6cbc20b25a0c93ec4d9d08b3", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[119]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0119", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Who’s he?’ asked Steerforth, in his careless way.", "sha256": "4d5345dbb9e4ccb6dc6e5bd4aae84b2d501c3c8e28733dd18f1a815c5f31ee95", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[120]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0120", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Don’t you remember Traddles? Traddles in our room at Salem House?’", "sha256": "9dca7b00571804c61644d20d3f358ef194910892a9560ad3a91a3ccd8cdb03b9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[121]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0121", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "‘Oh! That fellow!’ said Steerforth, beating a lump of coal on the top of the fire, with the poker. ‘Is he as soft as ever? And where the deuce did you pick him up?’", "sha256": "fe1fbeadfbcb3cf7cfc18cc22f659f6a5b559f9518bc6bb317d7aba7a7ff78a9", "source_xpath": "/html/body/div[35]/p[122]", "emphasis_spans": 0, "bold_spans": 0, "smallcaps_spans": 0, "note_markers": [], "source_class": ""}, {"id": "en85-u030-b0122", "tag": "p", "role": "paragraph", "text": "I extolled Traddles in reply, as highly as I could; for I felt that Steerforth rather slighted him. Steerforth, dismissing the subject with a light nod, and a smile, and the remark that he would be glad to see the old fellow too, for he had always been an odd fish, inquired if I could give him anything to eat? During most of this short dialogue, when he had not been speaking in a wild vivacious manner, he had sat idly beating on the lump of coal with the poker.
